why: Pages describe leaving the south glacier and a final snow and ice line, but none says whether crevasses are met on this face.
Two pages call the Twincicle Glacier short and incredibly steep with crampons needed, but neither mentions crevasses, a bergschrund or roping on it.
Parties cross the Dana Glacier to a bergschrund at the couloir base, and an accident report has a roped team falling on its steep ice with the bergschrund open.
The line crosses the Mendel Glacier and then a bergschrund where the glacier meets the couloir base, before roped ice climbing.
Pages only say to go up the glacier to the couloir with crampons and axe; no bergschrund, crevasse or roping is described.
The Isabelle Glacier upper part is described as probably just a perennial snowfield, and a July party climbed the snow with no rope or anchors and mentioned no crevasse or bergschrund.
Parties descend onto the Vesper Glacier, cross it to the face with a moat in late season and a crevasse noted, using ice axe, rope and harness.
